PullRequest.Title: Model router skill: learn the user's work from their recent chats
PullRequest.Body:
The model router skill now offers to learn what work the user does from their recent Copilot chats before it writes routes.

A router picks a route by matching each request against the routes' `when` text and examples. It works best when those name the work the user actually does, phrased the way they phrase it. Short requests that start real work, such as "fix it" or "why is this flaky?", are the ones most often sent to the wrong route.

New workflow steps:
- **Ask first.** Offer to look at the user's recent chats, and read them only if the user agrees.
- **Read only the user's messages.** Read the `user.message` events from the last few weeks in the host's session-state folder, ignoring the agent's replies and tool output. List the kinds of work, how often each comes up, and how the user phrases short requests and hand-offs.
- **Cover the frequent work.** Make sure every kind of work the user does often is named in some route's `when` or examples.
- **Don't copy details.** Write examples in the user's style, but never copy file paths, names, links or other details into the router, since router files may be shared.

The skill gets the session-state folder from the agent host's Copilot home, the same way it already gets the router folder, so the path is right on remote hosts too.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new critical-path scan and unbounded glob are explicit in the changed line, and the same source file directly establishes realistic per-file sizes. The exact delay depends on consent and the user's recent-session volume, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem reads, JSON parsing, and user-message bytes emitted into the agent context
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The work grows with every matching session and with the full byte size of each events.jsonl file; the glob provides no cap on session count, aggregate bytes, or extracted messages, and repeated router runs rescan the same history.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased router-creation latency, excessive disk I/O, and potentially large context/token processing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Creating or editing a model router did not inspect session logs, so this workflow incurred no history-wide filesystem scan before writing the router.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After the user agrees, the new mandatory workflow tells the agent to read user.message content across all session event logs from the last few weeks before it writes the router.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 322 is the first code that directs model-router creation to read every recent session log; before this line the workflow went directly from checking available models to writing the router.
Findings.Title: Bound and stream the recent-chat history scan
Findings.Impact: A user with many recent chats can make a one-time router setup scan many large files on its critical path; even one event log is documented in this same skill as potentially hundreds of MB, and the added instruction neither requires streaming nor caps extracted content, so setup can stall on disk/JSON work and flood the model context.
Findings.Evidence: The added workflow targets `session-state/*/events.jsonl` and requires aggregating message kinds and frequencies across them. The repository's adjacent Tooling Strategy at lines 207-210 explicitly warns that an individual `events.jsonl` can be hundreds of MB and must never be loaded whole, requiring a constant-memory streaming pass. That safety rule belongs only to the troubleshoot skill and is absent from the newly added model-router workflow. No cache, grouping, aggregate-byte limit, message limit, or concurrency limiter is introduced.
Findings.Recommendation: Change the skill to enumerate recent files first, impose explicit session/aggregate-byte/message limits, and use one streaming type-and-timestamp-filtered pass that emits only a bounded sample or incremental aggregate rather than loading or printing all message content.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or edit a model router after accepting recent-chat personalization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workflow first checks available models, then enumerates and analyzes recent session logs; that analysis must finish before routes are written and validated, so the newly added history work is on the setup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate session-state/*/events.jsonl and read/parse recent user.message records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory enumeration plus reads of every selected recent session log; total work is the sum of all log bytes, with individual logs documented in the same file as potentially hundreds of MB.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Router creation did not access session history, so it performed zero session-log filesystem reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The resulting work classification and phrasing analysis must complete before the router is written.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the model-router checking tool to list models and validate each edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one initial call and one validation call per edit, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial and per-edit validation calls were already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing calls already gate writing/completing the router; the new log scan adds latency between them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write or edit the router YAML through the agent's file tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one write plus corrections, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The router was written directly after model discovery without first scanning chat logs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to produce the router, after the newly added history analysis.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of session directories from the last few weeks and the aggregate bytes/events in their events.jsonl files, then the number and total content bytes of matching user.message events. There is no cap or deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The prompt specifies no shared limiter or batching strategy. An agent may serialize scans in one shell pass or issue multiple reads, but either way it processes the aggregate bytes of all selected logs; there is no coalescing across repeated router runs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no application cache or saved aggregate. Cold runs read from storage; warm runs may benefit only from the OS page cache, and each later invocation repeats enumeration, parsing, and message extraction. There is no negative-cache concern.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line explicitly requires the multi-file scan, and adjacent repository guidance states that each event log can reach hundreds of MB and must be streamed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Consent rate, session count, message sizes, storage speed, and whether a particular agent chooses streaming tools vary. These affect duration and prevalence, but one-file size and unbounded aggregate work are explicitly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity filesystem fan-out and context-allocation regression because the diff adds uncapped history-wide work to the critical path without the streaming and output bounds already required elsewhere for these files.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or edit a model router after declining recent-chat personalization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The agent skips the optional history analysis and continues through existing model discovery, router file editing, and validation; the changed session path is only text in the skill content and does not itself touch storage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List available models and validate the router.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two workflow calls, unchanged from before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same model discovery and validation calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing critical-path validation only; declining prevents the new history boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write or edit the router YAML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more edits, unchanged from before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Skill retrieval performs two replacements over a small constant template. Router validation scales only with the existing bounded router file (at most 32 KiB).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrent work is introduced; existing tool and file operations proceed in workflow order.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the constant-size string replacements. Existing router checks retain their prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: createCopilotSkillProvider.readSkill only substitutes paths, and no filesystem API is called there.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed path; only constant template replacement occurs when personalization is declined.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression in this branch because the new filesystem workflow is conditional on consent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and expose the model-router built-in skill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reading the skill returns its in-memory template after two path substitutions; no session log is opened during discovery or readSkill.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant template size and fixed two replacements per read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent provider reads can run concurrently without shared mutable state or expensive boundaries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache, but the operation is constant-size CPU/allocation work; cold and warm behavior are effectively equivalent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the complete changed function and call site inspection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed replacement is linear only in the small built-in template size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the additional string replacement is negligible and does not itself perform filesystem I/O.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Reported one introduced, consent-triggered unbounded session-log scan; rejected the constant template replacement and test changes as non-issues.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
